questions.stem: Convert $1011_2$ to a number in base ten.
questions.explanation: The place values from the right are $2^0 = 1$, $2^1 = 2$, $2^2 = 4$ and $2^3 = 8$. So $1011_2 = (1 \times 8) + (0 \times 4) + (1 \times 2) + (1 \times 1) = 8 + 2 + 1 = 11$.

distractorRationale.a: Missed the units digit, adding only 8 + 1
distractorRationale.c: Counted the zero column as a 2, adding an extra 2
distractorRationale.d: Copied the numeral instead of converting it

questions.stem: Express $324_5$ as a number in base ten.

distractorRationale.c: Multiplied the units digit by 5 as well
distractorRationale.d: Used 100 for the $5^2$ column, treating the base as ten

questions.stem: Convert $45_{10}$ to a number in base 2.
questions.explanation: Divide repeatedly by 2 and record remainders: 45 gives r1, 22 gives r0, 11 gives r1, 5 gives r1, 2 gives r0, 1 gives r1. Reading the remainders from the last to the first gives $101101_2$. Checking, $32 + 8 + 4 + 1 = 45$.

distractorRationale.a: Two remainders swapped; this numeral is worth 43
distractorRationale.c: Read the remainders downwards instead of upwards; this numeral is worth 53
distractorRationale.d: Placed the final remainder in the units column; this numeral is worth 46

questions.stem: Convert $29_{10}$ to a number in base 3.
questions.explanation: Divide by 3 repeatedly and keep the remainders: 29 gives r2, 9 gives r0, 3 gives r0, 1 gives r1. Reading upwards gives $1002_3$, and checking, $27 + 0 + 0 + 2 = 29$.

distractorRationale.b: Read the remainders downwards; this numeral is worth 55
distractorRationale.c: Put the remainder 2 in the threes column instead of the units column
distractorRationale.d: Contains the digit 9, which cannot appear in base 3 at all

questions.stem: Simplify $1101_2 + 111_2$, leaving your answer in base 2.
questions.explanation: In base ten the numbers are 13 and 7, so the sum is 20, and $20 = 16 + 4 = 10100_2$. Working directly in base 2 gives the same result: each column that reaches 2 carries 1 to the next column.

distractorRationale.a: Added the digits without carrying anything
distractorRationale.b: Lost one carry from the middle columns; this is 18
distractorRationale.d: Carried an extra 1 into the leading column; this is 28

questions.stem: Evaluate $423_5 - 144_5$, leaving your answer in base 5.
questions.explanation: Convert both to base ten: $423_5 = 100 + 10 + 3 = 113$ and $144_5 = 25 + 20 + 4 = 49$. The difference is 64, and $64 = (2 \times 25) + (2 \times 5) + 4 = 224_5$. Working column by column, each borrow is worth 5, not 10.

distractorRationale.b: Borrowed 10 instead of 5 in one column
distractorRationale.c: Subtracted in base ten and left the digits unconverted, producing the invalid digit 9
distractorRationale.d: Forgot to reduce the leading digit after borrowing

questions.stem: Evaluate $23_4 \times 3_4$, leaving your answer in base 4.
questions.explanation: In base ten $23_4 = 8 + 3 = 11$, so $11 \times 3 = 33$. Converting 33 to base 4: $33 = (2 \times 16) + (0 \times 4) + 1 = 201_4$.

distractorRationale.a: Multiplied the digits in base ten and never converted, leaving the invalid digits 6 and 9
distractorRationale.c: Carried in tens rather than fours; this numeral is worth 27
distractorRationale.d: Placed the carry one column too far left; this numeral is worth 39

questions.explanation: Expand the left side by place value: $3x + 4 = 28$. Subtracting 4 gives $3x = 24$, so $x = 8$. The digits 3 and 4 are both less than 8, so base 8 is valid.

distractorRationale.b: Divided 28 by 4 instead of isolating $3x$ first
distractorRationale.d: Added 4 to 28 before dividing, giving 32 over 3 rounded up

questions.stem: Convert $2103_4$ to base ten. Give a number only.
questions.explanation: The place values are $4^3 = 64$, $4^2 = 16$, $4^1 = 4$ and $4^0 = 1$. So the value is $(2 \times 64) + (1 \times 16) + (0 \times 4) + (3 \times 1) = 128 + 16 + 0 + 3 = 147$.

questions.stem: The numeral $152_5$ is a valid number in base 5.
questions.explanation: False. In base $n$ the only digits allowed are 0 up to $n - 1$, so base 5 can use only 0, 1, 2, 3 and 4. The digit 5 in $152_5$ makes the numeral impossible, because five units would be carried into the next column as one group of five.
